name: Barak
charge: Going down from Tabor at the word of the Lord against nine hundred chariots of iron; and going only on condition that Deborah went
summary: The Lord had already commanded Barak to march to mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, and Deborah was sent to remind him of it. He answered that he would go only if she went with him; she went, and told him the journey would not be for his honour, for the Lord would hand Sisera over to a woman. He went down anyway against nine hundred chariots of iron, and the Lord routed Sisera and all his army before him, until not a man was left. The record still counts him among the faithful.
offenseFull: Deborah called Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and asked whether the Lord God of Israel had not commanded him to march to mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, since the Lord would draw Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his troops to the river Kishon and give him into his hand (Judges 4:6-9). Read her words again. She is not handing him a new errand; she is asking whether God has not already told him to do this. The Lord had spoken to him, Barak was slow and fearful about it, and so the Lord spoke to His prophetess and sent her to confirm it to his face. Barak answered that he would go if she went with him, and if she would not go, he would not go. She said she would certainly go, but the journey would not be for his honour, because the Lord would hand Sisera over to a woman. The promise of victory stood; only the honour of the day was taken from him.

He called Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and went up with ten thousand men behind him, and Deborah went up with him (Judges 4:6-10). When she told him the day had come and asked whether the Lord had not gone out ahead of him, Barak went down from mount Tabor with ten thousand men after him. That was the test: horses, chariots and an army larger than his, and the word of the Lord telling him not to fear them, because the Lord his God was with him (Deuteronomy 20:1). The song remembers who stood with him. Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to the death on the heights of the field; those tribes are warriors. Set against them are the clans of Reuben, full of deep thoughts and heart searching, second guessing themselves, and Gilead staying across the Jordan, and Dan with the ships, and Asher on the coast (Judges 5:15-21).
judgmentFull: The Lord routed Sisera, all his chariots and all his army before Barak’s sword, and Barak chased the chariots and the army to Harosheth of the Gentiles, and the whole army of Sisera fell by the sword until not a man was left (Judges 4:14-16). Heaven itself fought; the stars from their courses battled Sisera, and the river Kishon swept them away (Judges 5:19-21). The pursuit was real work, but the victory was not in the arm that did it. When Barak came in pursuit, Jael came out to meet him and showed him the man he was looking for, lying dead with the tent peg in his temple (Judges 4:22). Both words spoken over him were fulfilled in one day: the army was given into his hand, and the honour of the captain went to a woman.

His hesitation cost him the honour; it did not cost Israel the deliverance, and it did not cost him his name. The record of the faithful still counts Barak among those who by faith conquered kingdoms, grew strong in battle, and put foreign armies to flight (Hebrews 11:32-34). That is worth weighing by any brother who has been called to something and is dragging his feet: the calling was already on him, the word came to him twice, and when he finally moved, God did exactly what He said He would do. Then Deborah and Barak sang that day, praising the Lord for avenging Israel when the people offered themselves willingly (Judges 5:1-2). The song ends by wishing ruin on the Lord’s enemies and the strength of the rising sun on those who love Him; and the land had rest forty years (Judges 5:31).

taught.title: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear
Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

text.text: And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh–naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not the Lord God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand.
And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the Lord shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh–naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not the Lord God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand.
And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the Lord shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and he went up with ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah went up with him.

When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; even Issachar, and also Barak: he was sent on foot into the valley. For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts of heart.
Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead abode beyond Jordan: and why did Dan remain in ships? Asher continued on the sea shore, and abode in his breaches.
Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field.
The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money.
They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
The river of Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength.

And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand: is not the Lord gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
And the Lord discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet.
But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, unto Harosheth of the Gentiles: and all the host of Sisera fell upon the edge of the sword; and there was not a man left.
The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money.
They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
The river of Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength.

And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.
And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,
Praise ye the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves.
So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.
